name: Peripheral Motor Neuropathy-Dysautonomia Syndrome
aliases: Peripheral Motor Neuropathy with Autonomic Dysfunction

criteria.description: Clinical evidence of peripheral motor neuropathy with distal muscle weakness and atrophy
Presence of autonomic dysfunction including orthostatic hypotension, abnormal sweating, or gastrointestinal dysmotility
Electrophysiological studies demonstrating reduced motor nerve conduction velocities and denervation potentials
Exclusion of other causes of motor neuropathy and dysautonomia such as diabetes or amyloidosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical peripheral motor neuropathy and autonomic dysfunction confirmed by electrophysiological studies, with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including neurology and autonomic testing

searchTerms: EMG showing nerve or muscle problems

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests excluding diabetes and autoimmune markers
CSF analysis typically normal or mildly elevated protein
imaging: MRI of spine to exclude structural causes of neuropathy
Autonomic function testing including tilt-table test
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; genetic testing to exclude hereditary neuropathies
other: Electromyography showing denervation and reduced motor unit potentials
Nerve conduction studies demonstrating reduced motor conduction velocities

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness with respiratory compromise
Signs of systemic amyloidosis or malignancy
references: Dyck PJ, Thomas PK. Peripheral Neuropathy. 4th ed. Elsevier Saunders; 2005.
Low PA. Autonomic Neurology. In: Bradley WG, Daroff RB, Fenichel GM, Jankovic J, editors. Neurology in Clinical Practice. 6th ed. Butterworth-Heinemann; 2012.
